notes: Documentary letters of credit are the dominant payment instrument for lighter imports. LC coupling ratio ~0.95 because the physical shipment is the document trigger. Minimal decoupling risk in this layer.

claim_counterparty: US/EU mass-market retailers (Walmart; Dollar Tree; Tesco)
source_name: NACS State of the Industry 2023; retailer annual reports (estimated)
notes: Retailer private-label sourcing agreements vs actual sell-through. Coupling ratio ~0.70 because agreements are non-binding volume estimates. Retailer has right to substitute product; reduce orders without penalty. Inventory risk sits with distributor. This is the first material E-layer stress point.

source_name: BIC Group Annual Report 2023; UN Comtrade HS 9613 declared values (inferred)
notes: BIC brand premium claim: the BIC Classic retails at $1.49 vs $0.89 for an identical generic OEM unit. The physical product is functionally identical (same ISO 9994 compliance; same butane; same ferrocerium flint). The $0.60 premium ($0.40 per unit = 67% premium) is entirely abstract value — the brand claim. Coupling ratio ~0.60 (physical value $0.89; abstract claim $1.49). This is the PRIMARY E-LAYER FINDING for the lighter supply chain: the only meaningful abstract decoupling occurs at the retail brand premium layer. It confirms the theoretical prediction that in a commodity with near-zero manufacturing cost variation the only available rent is at the brand abstraction layer.
